short: verb modules and shared exit codes
is: One module per verb that runs the app use case, prints terse, --json or --more output, and maps the outcome to the shared exit codes.
conventions: One file per verb named after it; a verb module owns printing and the exit code, the logic stays in app
Exit codes for every verb: 0 ok, 1 domain refusal, 2 backend failure or missing, 64 listed but not built; clap keeps 2 for usage errors
Instance verbs read ZAF_INSTANCE (`<role> instance <n> on #<epic>`) and slice verbs ZAF_VERSION; the spawner sets both

fs.name: ask.rs
fs.role: ask and print the verified answer; exit 2 when a citation fails its check

fs.name: asklog.rs
fs.role: asklog: the pages cited most, the questions that keep returning, the gaps

fs.name: begin.rs
fs.role: `zaf begin --version <v>`: exit 2 with one sentence inside an instance or without a terminal; draws the release's four stages (✓ done, ▸ here) and asks `Open it? [Y/n]` (n: `Nothing changed.`, exit 0), runs the due phase's action (objectives or design) on the terminal, checks what the session left, prints `✓ <file> written`, asks `Sign it? ... [Y/n]` (type-ahead dropped first; Enter, y or yes signs, n does not, anything else asks again) and, on a yes, prints `✓ <file> signed` and goes on to what is due next; with --json none of the screen is drawn; exit 1 only when the action failed, something is missing or the document is left unsigned (`Not signed.`; exit 2 when the action never ran); at the build stage (every open epic signed, one not done; not with --json) it draws the stages with the fourth marked and asks `Every epic of <v> is signed. Start the build now? [Y/n]`: y execs `zaf spawn --watch --version <v>` in place (exit 2 if it cannot start), n or closed input prints that command and exits 0; at the built stage (every open epic done) it draws the four stages done, runs `release-open` and prints the release pull request with `zaf begin --version <next>`; exit 0 when nothing else is due: at the epics stage (an open epic unsigned) it draws the four stages with Epics marked, `The design became <n> epics`, each epic with its ticket count (or `zaf plans its tickets once you sign it`) over `read zaf epic show <n>   sign zaf epic sign <n>` (`signed` for a signed one) and the `zaf spawn --watch --version <v>` line, with --json the epics as JSON

fs.name: begin/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: board.rs
fs.role: board actions; a question asked inside a phase run (ZAF_RUN) of its own task is recorded in the run folder's `questions`

fs.name: brief.rs
fs.role: write the pack, print path and token estimate

fs.name: changes.rs
fs.role: changes: a task's change against its base, stat first, hunks with --path

fs.name: check.rs
fs.role: check and verify; stores records under .zaf/runs/

fs.name: do_action.rs
fs.role: `zaf do`: list the actions the caller may read, run one, or print the file a name resolves to; exit 0 prints nothing

fs.name: doctor.rs
fs.role: ShellCommands backing doctor's Commands; asks the composed board and forge their access checks (no [forge], no forge checks), for setup's doctor run too

fs.name: epic.rs
fs.role: zaf epic file --version <v> --title <t>: the body on stdin, prints the epic's id; an empty title or body, or a board that cannot file an epic, exits 1. zaf epic list|sign: one line per open epic, or `signed #<n> sha256:<hex>`; exit 1 inside an instance or for no open epic; a signature that cannot ask the running scheduler for a tick stays signed and says so in one line on stderr; a signature that is the last of its version's epics, at a terminal outside an instance and without --json, asks `Every epic of <v> is signed. Start the build now? [Y/n]`, and yes execs `zaf spawn --watch --version <v>` from PATH in place (exit 2 if it cannot start), no or closed input exits 0

fs.name: exit.rs
fs.role: exit codes, port and composition error mapping

fs.name: forge.rs
fs.role: zaf forge open|merge|checks|head|log: the number then the link (base optional: the forge's default branch), nothing, `<bucket>\t<name>\t<link>` lines, the head, the log block; exit 1 refused, 2 backend or no [forge]

fs.name: guard.rs
fs.role: guard: computes the budget level and writes .zaf/guard.json

fs.name: guard/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: hub.rs
fs.role: `zaf hub`, `zaf hub report` and `zaf hub link`, and the reports the other verbs leave; in a terminal it waits and redraws on a new report

fs.name: hub/
fs.role: the loop that feeds the LAN page, the service verbs, and the tick and watch the page's controls run

fs.name: mcp.rs
fs.role: the MCP server's CLI layer: the tool catalog read from clap's verbs

fs.name: mcp/
fs.role: catalog.rs (the visible verbs as tools, and the line checker over clap) and its tests

fs.name: profile.rs
fs.role: profile init: the hermetic Claude profiles under .zaf/profiles/

fs.name: progress.rs
fs.role: `zaf progress`: a model declares its phases on a task and reports each change, one hub report a call

fs.name: report.rs
fs.role: report: tokens per model, the subagent growth profile, the per-run table

fs.name: report/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: scheduler.rs
fs.role: `spawn --watch`: the scheduler that stays up; takes scheduler.lock (a second one names the first and exits 1), catches SIGINT and SIGTERM, and runs app/schedule/scheduler.rs with this process as its Host: requests, the timer, the binary look and exec, the lock-held wait, the start, restart and stop lines; a scheduler fresh on the lock first runs the build start (app/build.rs): `made <branch>` or `<branch> is open`, then `committed <id>`, a refusal on stderr with the lock let go and exit 1 (2 for a backend), and a restart or a take-over skips it

fs.name: screen.rs
fs.role: the screen kit: Screen::detect (colour only for a terminal stdout, NO_COLOR unset or empty, TERM not dumb; redraw for a terminal and TERM not dumb), paint(Meaning, text) with the mocks' codes, program(text), which colours each whole word `zaf` and never one in a path or a longer word, and ask_yes(screen, prompt, default, input, output), the yes-or-no question: Enter takes the default, y and yes are yes, anything starting with n is no, anything else is asked again, closed input is no, the choices painted as Done; on a terminal it first discards what was typed ahead

fs.name: screen/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: setup.rs
fs.role: setup: asks for a missing manifest, moves a root ZAF.toml, makes the two homes, generates the profiles, then hands the Engineer what it cannot do

fs.name: slice.rs
fs.role: slice actions plus helpers changes shares

fs.name: spawn.rs
fs.role: one tick: the phase steps 3 to 6 first, on the phased tasks, with the machine's budget, then the planning and challenger launches joined in parallel threads; --dry-run, whose --json carries the core's `placement`; a real tick appends its trace line (where each ticket sits, what it did, what moved) and prints each move and a count, --json gaining `moved` and `tickets`; the tick's zaf-kind runner, whose run leaves a phase run folder opened through the gate again (NOT_RUN 125 when refused), and its wait and model-phase starter (zaf spawn phase, never waiting for the phase); `--once` asks a running scheduler instead of ticking; one_tick is the tick the scheduler runs, naming who asked and keeping the placement in its cache

fs.name: spawn_phase.rs
fs.role: `spawn phase` (starts a detached launcher, returns at once) and the hidden `spawn phase-run` launcher that runs the action, waits, then records the head it left (`head-end`) and its exit, then asks for a tick: a request to the running scheduler, else `spawn --once --no-wait`

fs.name: spawn_start.rs
fs.role: `spawn start --version <v>`: starts the project's scheduler detached through the app-layer start and prints its pid and log; a scheduler already holding the lock is handed back with its pid and nothing is started (both exit 0); an invalid version exits 1, a start that failed exits 2; --json gives pid, started, log

fs.name: spawn_stop.rs
fs.role: `spawn stop <task>`: ends the instance running the task and every process of its group (terminate, then kill after a grace) and releases its claim; exit 1 when none runs

fs.name: spawn_trace.rs
fs.role: `spawn trace [<ticket>] [--since <when>]`: the moves of the trace, oldest first, with the date when they cross a day; --more adds what each tick did; read-only, no lock; no trace yet says so and exits 0

fs.name: status.rs
fs.role: status: board, instances, slots, guard and open questions on one screen, with every live zaf instance of the machine; with [phases], where the core places each ticket

fs.name: status/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: steps.rs
fs.role: ScreenSteps, the terminal's StepReport: on a live screen a thread draws a braille spinner beside the row's verb and noun every 80 ms, and ended replaces the line (`\r\x1b[K`) with ✓ or ✗ and the end's text; on any other screen only the final line, with no `\r` and no escape byte when colour is off; the thread is joined on ended and on drop

fs.name: steps/
fs.role: tests.rs

fs.name: tests.rs
fs.role: parsing and exit-64 tests

fs.name: update.rs
fs.role: zaf update [--check|--yes]: GitHub releases of ProgrammingCheetah/ways, one line on a change, exit 1 on a check that finds a newer release; --yes runs the plan with the Assumed answers, no terminal, ends on one line naming what was replaced and kept, exit 2 on a failed step, nothing changed inside an instance

fs.name: watch_view.rs
fs.role: the live view of `spawn --watch` in a terminal (stdin and stdout a terminal, no --json, TERM not dumb): a thread that redraws app/spawn/view.rs's frame in place on the normal screen, reads the window's size before each frame, gathers the project's state after each tick and on each hub report and between those turns the spinner; while it is up stdout and stderr are `.zaf/logs/scheduler.log`, a failed tick is one line naming it, `stty -echo` is on and put back (with the output) on every way out: the drop, a panic hook, the restart's drop before the exec

notes: Verbs: board (ready, claim, report, handoff, question, ruling), ask, brief, check, verify, changes, slice (open, pr, merge, drop), spawn (phase, stop, trace), asklog, status, report, guard, doctor, setup, profile init, do, hub (report, link, service install|remove), progress (plan, at), update, epic (list, show, sign, file), begin, forge (open, merge, checks, head, log)
`init` is not a verb: `setup` asks the manifest questions through app/init.rs
check.rs names adapters directly (SystemShell, gate RUNS_DIR), the only non-test place outside composition.rs that does
